name: Ozaki Hōsai 尾崎放哉
credit: Photograph of Ozaki Hōsai · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons); texts from the Aozora Bunko selection (card 974)
bio: 尾崎放哉 (Ozaki Hōsai, 1885–1926) was born Ozaki Hideo in Tottori. He studied law at Tokyo Imperial University and worked for years in insurance, but drink and quarrels cost him his post, his marriage and his place in society. He gave up that life, joined the Ittōen community in Kyoto, and then lived as a temple caretaker at Sumadera, in Obama, and finally on Shōdoshima in the Inland Sea, where he died of tuberculosis in 1926.

With Taneda Santōka he is counted the chief poet of free-verse haiku, a pupil of Ogiwara Seisensui who dropped the 5-7-5 measure and the seasonal word. His poems of solitude, poverty and illness, among them the famous せきをしてもひとり, are very short and plain. This selection of fifty draws on the Aozora Bunko edition and favours the mature years at Sumadera, Obama, Kyoto and Shōdoshima.
